proposal.name: Bound conformance memory and split exhausted batches

issue_plan.name: Bound conformance memory and split exhausted batches
issue_plan.summary: Three ordered plumbing changes put state and attempt contents on disk while allowing small fixed-size indexes in memory, connect the gate's recording producers to the streaming checker, and split memory-exhausted batches before using the exclusive retry. They preserve conformance verdicts, counterexamples, strict-attempt rules and diagnostics, and record splits in the existing resource history. Each change updates SPEC.md and docs/gate.md to describe the behavior it actually delivers. The merger records the new storage and split policies in the decision journal; the plumbing builds do not write decisions/.

issues.title: Check conformance recordings incrementally with bounded disk-backed storage
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Part 1 of issue #549. The conformance checker currently decodes an entire recording, keeps canonical state text in an index and states slice plus readable text in pretty, and retains every transition and attempt. In the 2026-11-04 factory/recovery gate this contributed to a watcher reaching 61 GB on a 48 GB machine. Replace the checker-owned recording representation so memory is a small fixed-size entry per distinct state, transition and attempt, plus the active batches and bounded working storage.

Add a streaming input entry point in internal/conformance and retain the existing Check(..., raw []byte, ...) behavior as a compatibility wrapper. Parse both sampled traces and states/init/attempts incrementally, including declared fifth-field outcomes. Keep each distinct canonical state's text once on disk in compact private temporary storage; derive readable diagnostics only when needed. Fixed-size entries may stay in memory, including a state-hash-to-offset index, the original-state-ID mapping, starts, transition pairs to sort, and attempt offsets and ordering. Anything whose size grows with a state's or an attempt's contents must stay on disk outside the active batches and bounded working storage: canonical and readable state text, decoded values, action names, arguments and outcomes, including the contents of per-state tried-action sets. Read only the contents a batch needs and keep caches bounded. Exact canonical equality must determine deduplication even if hashing is used. Preserve first-seen state identities, sorted transition ordering and original strict-attempt ordering.

Generate Init, Next, strict-attempt and every-step-tried obligations from bounded windows of that store. A step batch receives only its endpoint states, with local indexes; tried checks receive only their states and attempted actions. Bound starting-state processing as well, so many distinct starts cannot recreate a whole-recording allocation. Keep the ordinary 2,000-step/strict-attempt and 1,000-state tried batch limits and bounded concurrency. Keep model module copies available in isolated batch directories. Generate and schedule batches lazily; do not retain one closure, cancellation function or decoded batch per future batch. Because the byte-input compatibility wrapper also uses the new checker, adapt internal/verify/python_application_gate.go's ordered model-runner adapter in this same change for bounded initial-state batches; preserve its deterministic failure prefix and cover it in python_application_gate_numbers_test.go. This must work before the producer integration in part 2. This issue does not introduce adaptive memory retries: the existing TLC retry policy stays in force until part 3.

Preserve the complete Result and Tried contracts: counts, legacy stuttering, exact integers, canonical sets/functions/records, named action and argument checks, enabled read-only actions, refusal disabledness and changed-state refusals. Distinct declared actions, arguments and outcomes sharing a state pair must still be checked individually. Preserve the earliest failing batch's diagnostic despite later batches completing first, and map local counterexample indexes back to the correct original states and attempt. A strict failure must not earn tried coverage. Malformed recordings retain their existing refusal messages and validation precedence and must not reach TLC. Account for arbitrary top-level field order, attempts before states, repeated fields under the existing JSON rules, absent/null versus empty attempts, trailing data, out-of-range references, invalid states and arguments, and duplicate keys in declared outcome metadata. Do not tighten legacy duplicate-key handling as a side effect.

Storage and input errors are operational errors, never successful or partial conformance evidence. Context cancellation must stop decoding, iteration and scheduling, join started checks, and close and remove private temporary storage on success, semantic refusal, tool error or cancellation. Do not remove the caller's model or recording. Several invocations must not share temporary stores.

Read and preserve the behavior in internal/conformance/conformance_test.go, batches_accept_test.go, declared_refusal_accept_test.go, declared_refusal_regression_test.go, python_application_numbers_accept_test.go, tried_integration_test.go and declared_refusal_integration_test.go. In particular, acceptTLC reads emitted modules, checks real copied Counter/Limit files, parses local state/pair indexes, and deliberately finishes later bad batches first. TestDecodeReadsAttempts inspects the current private representation and may need an equivalent test of the new store rather than retaining that representation. Any existing test requiring edits must be named in this issue's eventual file plan.

Acceptance must exercise the streaming entry point through the checker, not just a decoder or database. Generate file-backed large recordings without constructing them in the measured process's heap; use isolated measurements with fixed concurrency and a meaningful fixed peak-heap ceiling that allows for the permitted fixed-size entries. Use states large enough that the old whole-recording implementation exceeds that ceiling. Doubling distinct states at that state size and batch size must stay within the same ceiling. Exercise both traces and attempts, many distinct starts, and many attempts over few states so state deduplication alone cannot pass. Measure decoding and all checking phases, not only live heap after a forced final GC. Verify exact expected results and complete obligation coverage with a bounded-memory semantic TLC stand-in. Add compatibility cases for a passing recording, bad start, bad step, earliest failure ordering, untried action, and declared accepted/refused attempts the named model action rejects, plus exact malformed-input messages. Test short reads, read errors, cancellation and temporary-store cleanup. The stand-in must validate the emitted obligations and must not itself retain the whole recording.

Update SPEC.md and docs/gate.md in this change to describe the streaming checker, its memory and temporary-disk costs and cleanup, and explicitly distinguish this new entry point from gate callers that are connected in part 2. The memory bound is a small fixed-size entry per distinct state, transition and attempt, plus the active batches and bounded working storage. It is not a promise that an arbitrarily large individual state, attempt or model fits in a fixed number of bytes. The README already links docs/gate.md; keep detailed explanation there.

This is tested plumbing under D-0105. Preserve the conformance and attempts rules grounded in D-0029, D-0047, D-0082, D-0085, D-0088 and D-0090, the declared-outcome behavior of #392, and the existing TLC budget/retry foundations D-0315, D-0306 and D-0322. D-0122 and D-0294 require current-state documentation. Cite recorded foundations on every changed SPEC bullet and reference this issue's ratified plan for the new behavior. The bounded-storage choice needs a new recorded decision: the merger records it, and the plumbing build does not edit decisions/. Run the affected Go tests and concurrency/race regressions. Unavailable Docker/network integration checks belong in Merger work; affected real Python and TLAPS opt-in suites run in PR CI.

issues.title: Stream gate recordings into the bounded conformance checker
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Part 2 of issue #549, after the disk-backed streaming conformance checker has merged. Connect the actual gate to that checker so a watcher running a final gate no longer reads a driver's entire recording into []byte before checking it. A reader API alone does not fix the incident: internal/verify/language.go currently reads traces.json for Go explorers and Python/TypeScript drivers, existing.go does the same for existing TypeScript, and verify.go retains Evidence.Traces until conformance begins.

Give the gate an owned file/stream path through recording production, evidence handoff and conformance consumption. Keep the recording alive after its producer's temporary workspace would otherwise be removed; close and remove it after consumption or any early exit, including unrelated gate errors and context cancellation. Do not leave an open file per queued batch or copy a recording through an in-memory buffer. Preserve the existing Language.Check/Evidence.Traces byte-returning compatibility behavior for callers that explicitly use it; the normal verify.Run path, including the factory's in-process final gate, must choose the streaming path for built-in producers. Cover Go Try exploration, ordinary Python and TypeScript drivers and existing TypeScript. A Go explorer without Try still supplies agreement alone. Preserve missing-recording and failed-driver messages and the distinction between absent evidence and a malformed or empty recording.

The existing Python-application gate also calls conformance.Check after pythonApplicationTraces or pythonApplicationAttempts builds a whole JSON document. Connect sampled and explored application conformance to the streaming checker, producing the transport incrementally and using disk-backed indexing where conversion requires deduplication. Keep module-value conversion, exact integers, replay filtering, declared outcomes, invocation identity and authenticated-observation validation unchanged. Do not change the direct Python.Check byte-returning contract or discard raw ordered observations, hashes or provenance required in application receipts. This task bounds the additional conformance transport/checking storage; the existing application receipt's retained raw observations remain evidence and must be accounted for honestly when documenting total gate memory. No second recording-sized tree or JSON buffer may be created for checking those observations.

Read the producers and consumers in internal/verify/language.go, existing.go, verify.go, python_application_gate.go and python_application_exploration.go, along with their cleanup and staging callers. Existing evidence compatibility is pinned by python_deps_accept_test.go, python_application_gate_accept_test.go, python_application_explore_cases_accept_test.go, python_hash_seed_accept_test.go and the Python authority/failure tests. Do not rewrite those byte-returning expectations to make the public API silently stop returning evidence. Read explorer_integration_test.go, harness_integration_test.go, verify_integration_test.go and the gate's fake Docker coverage in tlc_resources_accept_test.go. Those fakes recognize the /out mount, INVARIANT_TRACES=/out/traces.json and sandbox completion markers; preserve the driver environment, seeds, commands, flags, sandbox boundaries and marker interpretation. Name every existing test that actually needs adaptation in the eventual file plan.

Acceptance must run through verify.Run with a command-boundary driver/TLC stand-in and file-backed large recordings. It must demonstrate that doubling distinct states at fixed batch size and concurrency stays within the same meaningful peak-heap ceiling from production/hand-off through decoding and checking; allocate test data outside the measured process. Check exact expected gate/conformance counts and verdicts for both sizes, with a late bad step so the whole recording must be read. Cover Go Try and the ordinary driver route; verify the other producers use the same owned streaming handoff. A second case must prove many refused attempts over few states do not accumulate in host memory. Check retained file availability when conformance starts, cleanup after successful and failed gates and cancellation, missing output and failed-driver diagnostics, and unchanged agreement-only behavior. Add sampled/explored existing-Python cases preserving raw receipt evidence, strict-refusal behavior and JSON round-trip fingerprints while avoiding a second recording-sized transport allocation.

Update SPEC.md and docs/gate.md to describe the now-connected gate, the active-batch and bounded-store memory requirement, temporary disk proportional to recording data, ownership/cleanup, and the distinction between checker memory, TLC containers, driver execution and receipt evidence. Keep the README's linked reference page authoritative rather than adding implementation detail to the front page. Record measured ceilings and test conditions accurately; do not promise constant memory for unrelated retained report evidence.

Preserve D-0024, D-0029, D-0047, D-0054, D-0082, D-0085, D-0090 and the Python execution/evidence rules D-0181, D-0183, D-0185, D-0199 and D-0200, including #392's declared refusals. Build on the bounded-storage decision recorded when part 1 merges; D-0105, D-0122 and D-0294 govern tested implementation and current-state docs. Changed SPEC bullets cite recorded foundations and this issue's ratified plan. The merger records any new evidence-ownership implementation decision; the build does not write decisions/. Run affected Go tests, including compatibility and fingerprint suites. Real Python and TLAPS opt-in suites affected by shared gate changes run in PR CI; other unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work.

issues.title: Split conformance batches on memory exhaustion before exclusive retry
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Part 3 of issue #549, after streaming conformance storage and its gate integration have merged. A normal TLC allocation is currently a 2 GiB container with a 1536 MiB Java heap when capacity allows. Under #540/D-0322, any confirmed memory failure can immediately queue an exclusive retry using all known Docker memory after the quarter reserve. On factory/recovery, 44 of 76 conformance batches needed that retry. For a divisible conformance obligation, split the batch instead so smaller checks can continue at ordinary allocations alongside other work.

On confirmed Java memory exhaustion, finish cleanup and release the parent batch's ordinary slot, then replace it with two nonempty contiguous halves. Divide odd sizes without dropping or duplicating an item. Regenerate each half from the disk-backed store, carrying only its own states and local indexes; recurse if a half also exhausts memory. Apply this to ordinary step batches and strict-attempt batches, preserving each declared attempt independently. Starting-state and tried-state batches introduced or streamed in part 1 also split by their state units; an indivisible obligation is one step, one declared attempt or one state respectively. Only an indivisible conformance obligation that still exhausts its ordinary allocation may use the existing one-time exclusive retry. Unrelated design, witness, property, known-bug, larger-model and graph checks retain their existing retry policy.

Use an explicit runner capability or typed outcome for confirmed exhaustion and suppression of automatic escalation for divisible work. Do not infer it from arbitrary user-facing message substrings, module names or exit 137. Preserve TLC's existing classification, including frames 1001/1002/1003 and #552's wrapped ExecutionException with an OutOfMemoryError cause. No partial counterexample or success from an exhausted attempt may become evidence. Ordinary errors, actual counterexamples, stalls, cancellation and exit 137 without a confirming diagnostic must not split. Unknown Docker capacity and standalone runners still split divisible work at their ordinary limits, but cannot gain an exclusive allocation.

Keep scheduling bounded and demand-driven. Halves use the shared budget's ordinary FIFO admission, can overlap independent batches up to the established concurrency limit, and never reserve the whole budget or hold a parent slot while waiting for children. An OOM parent is pending recovery, not a semantic failure that cancels useful work. Preserve earliest failing batch ordering and the original logical item order across halves; map counterexamples back to the exact original bad start/step or named attempt and retain existing user-facing verdict diagnostics. Only completed leaves can settle a split obligation. Cancellation and deadlines stop the entire split tree, join cleanup, and start no further children or exclusive retry. Splitting must not renew the original execution allowance. Keep the existing one-stall-retry behavior for each check; an identical retry or singleton escalation must not renew it. Single-unit exclusive retries retain cleanup-before-admission, FIFO fairness, allocation rounding, headroom rules and exhaustion behavior.

Integrate this with the existing Python-application wrapper in internal/verify/python_application_gate.go. It currently derives order from steps-N/strict-N/tried-N directory names, serializes calls and marks every failed call terminal. It must understand logical parent/child completion without deadlocks or treating a recovered OOM as OperationalError. Preserve deterministic logical evidence, invocation provenance, counts, strict-attempt coverage and stable fingerprints; failed parent attempts and schedule-dependent recovery detail belong to operational history. Preserve the existing deterministic failure-prefix behavior where it is pinned by python_application_gate_numbers_test.go. Distinguish actual completed child evidence from the aggregate logical obligation without inventing model-check counts or hashing a failed attempt as successful evidence.

Extend tlc_attempts resource history so a person can reconstruct the split: retain the failed parent's allocation and diagnostic, identify its logical range/count, link both children to it, and retain every child's allocation, outcome and any later split or exclusive retry. Use portable unique identities, including repeated same-module batches; preserve JSON round trips and detached history snapshots. Show the split relationship and reason in verify feedback and Markdown receipts. Operational split/retry history remains outside evidence fingerprints, as D-0322 requires; existing reports without split fields remain readable. A recovered split must not change an otherwise identical successful gate's evidence fingerprint.

Read internal/tlc/tlc.go and resources.go; internal/conformance/conformance.go and tried.go and the streaming store added in part 1; internal/verify/python_application_gate.go, verify.go and feedback.go; and internal/receipt/receipt.go. Before naming files, inspect the command-boundary fakes and pinned assertions in internal/verify/large_tlc_540_accept_test.go, tlc_resources_accept_test.go, tlc_python_history_regression_test.go and python_application_gate_numbers_test.go, plus internal/tlc/memory_retry_regression_test.go, admission_regression_test.go, resources_regression_test.go, memory_frames_regression_test.go, wrapped_memory_552_accept_test.go, wrapped_memory_regression_test.go, stall_accept_test.go and stall_regression_test.go. Also preserve the semantic/concurrent batch tests and strict-refusal tests in internal/conformance. In particular, the two verify memory-history files currently require multi-step conformance batches to jump from 2 GiB to 12 GiB: intentionally replace only those conformance expectations with splitting, retaining ordinary model-check escalation assertions. Any existing test whose private API or fake must change must be named in the eventual file plan.

Acceptance must exercise actual tlc.Runner allocation and cleanup using a fake Docker executable, not merely a runner that returns an OOM string. A batch larger than the fake's ordinary-memory threshold must split into two complete halves, halve again if needed, run at the original --memory/--memory-swap/-Xmx limits while an unrelated ordinary check is active, and produce the same result as an unsplit reference check. Cover odd counts and verify each leaf obligation exactly once, batch-local states, a bad step in a right-hand descendant with correct original endpoints, and an earlier bad batch that completes after a later one. Repeat for strict accepted and refused attempts, including identical state pairs with different arguments/outcomes. Cover starting/tried-state splits and retain bad-start and untried-state diagnostics. A singleton must get precisely the existing exclusive retry with unchanged configuration, after other active allocations and cleanup drain. Cover persistent singleton exhaustion, no headroom, unknown capacity, wrapped memory diagnostics, non-memory failures, exit 137, cancellation/deadlines during recovery and stalled attempts without unbounded retries. Assert parent/child history in gate JSON, feedback and receipts, round-trip compatibility and unchanged successful fingerprints for ordinary and explicit/legacy existing-Python gates.

Update SPEC.md and docs/gate.md in the same change: explain halving, ordinary concurrent allocations, singleton-only conformance escalation, resource history, memory/disk bounds and preservation of the generic runner's policy for indivisible non-conformance checks. The README's linked gate page holds this detail. This intentionally refines D-0322 for divisible conformance batches, while retaining D-0315's budget, D-0306's stall rules and D-0111's cleanup. It also rests on D-0029, D-0047, D-0085, D-0090, D-0185, D-0199, #392's strict-attempt rules and the preceding bounded-storage decision. D-0105 makes it plumbing; D-0122 and D-0294 require accurate current-state documentation. Cite recorded foundations and this issue's ratified plan on changed SPEC bullets. The merger records the new split policy and its refinement of the retry decision; do not write decisions/ from the build. Run affected Go suites with race and repeated/shuffled scheduling coverage. Affected real Python and TLAPS opt-in suites run in PR CI; other unavailable Docker/network integration checks and decision recording belong in Merger work.

usage.summary: Wrote [issues.json](/var/folders/fz/s3p17rl97r30y73d180fjbmc0000gn/T/invariant-plan-450263075/issues.json), revising part 1 to allow fixed-size indexes in memory and require large-state heap tests. Parts 2 and 3 remain unchanged and in order; the plan passed its check.
